problem.problem:
Charlie is blue. Charlie is quiet. Dave is blue. Dave is cold. Dave is young. Erin is blue. Erin is quiet. Erin is white. Erin is young. Gary is cold. Gary is quiet. Gary is young. All quiet things are furry. If Charlie is cold then Charlie is young. White things are cold. All young things are nice. If Gary is nice then Gary is young. If something is young then it is nice. If something is furry and blue then it is white. If something is young and furry then it is nice.

Determine whether the following statement is true, false, or unknown:
Charlie is nice.

Predicates:
Blue($x, bool) ::: Is x blue?
Quiet($x, bool) ::: Is x quiet?
Cold($x, bool) ::: Is x cold?
Young($x, bool) ::: Is x young?
White($x, bool) ::: Is x white?
Furry($x, bool) ::: Is x furry?
Nice($x, bool) ::: Is x nice?

Facts:
Blue(Charlie, True) ::: Charlie is blue.
Quiet(Charlie, True) ::: Charlie is quiet.
Blue(Dave, True) ::: Dave is blue.
Cold(Dave, True) ::: Dave is cold.
Young(Dave, True) ::: Dave is young.
Blue(Erin, True) ::: Erin is blue.
Quiet(Erin, True) ::: Erin is quiet.
White(Erin, True) ::: Erin is white.
Young(Erin, True) ::: Erin is young.
Cold(Gary, True) ::: Gary is cold.
Quiet(Gary, True) ::: Gary is quiet.
Young(Gary, True) ::: Gary is young.

Rules:
Quiet($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: All quiet things are furry.
Cold(Charlie, True) >>> Young(Charlie, True) ::: If Charlie is cold then Charlie is young.
White($x, True) >>> Cold($x, True) ::: White things are cold.
Young($x, True) >>> Nice($x, True) ::: All young things are nice.
Nice(Gary, True) >>> Young(Gary, True) ::: If Gary is nice then Gary is young.
Young($x, True) >>> Nice($x, True) ::: If something is young then it is nice.
Furry($x, True) && Blue($x, True) >>> White($x, True) ::: If something is furry and blue then it is white.
Young($x, True) && Furry($x, True) >>> Nice($x, True) ::: If something is young and furry then it is nice.

Query:
Nice(Charlie, True) ::: Charlie is nice.
